key_facts: Pew Research Center reports about 3,000 data centres currently operate in the US, with that number potentially doubling in the next few years. Data centres are sited through local rules and permits, limiting federal lawmakers' direct influence.

During the first months of this year, community groups opposing data centres more than doubled to 833, according to Data Center Watch. Brookings Institution research found a new data centre creates 100-200 local jobs, 'fewer than industry advocates claim', with essentially no impact on local wages.

Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs enacted a three-year pause on new tax breaks for data centre projects in July. Recent polls found a majority of Ohio voters oppose data centres; Republican Senator John Husted has softened his support, while Democrat Sherrod Brown opposes new data centres and leads Husted in recent polls.

New national polling shows AI regulation and data centres are among top voter issues this election cycle, behind the ongoing Iran War and aspects of the economy. Trump has called the backlash a 'sick conspiracy'.
importance_reason: Политический и регуляторный тренд с потенциальным влиянием на инвестиции в AI-инфраструктуру и энергетику, но без прямого рыночного события и без цифр уровня макрорешений.
market_link: Ограничения и паузы на налоговые льготы и разрешения для дата-центров могут замедлить капитальные расходы на AI-инфраструктуру и спрос на электроэнергию, генерацию и чипы; прямой эффект на котировки пока не зафиксирован.
